national_raw_news.title: 5 hours ago | National 131 PM-SETU completes one year, aims to modernise Government ITIs
national_raw_news.content: Pradhan Mantri Skilling and Employability Transformation through Upgraded ITIs (PM-SETU) has completed one year today. The PM-SETU scheme of the Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship was launched on 4th of October last year. The initiative seeks to strengthen industry-led governance, upgrade training infrastructure and promote demand-driven courses in line with evolving workforce requirements. It aims to enhance the overall quality and relevance of vocational training by transforming Government India’s Industrial Training Institutes (ITIs) into modern, industry-aligned training institutions. The scheme has a total outlay of over 60 thousand crore rupees, comprising 30 thousand crore rupees from the Centre, 20 thousand crore rupees from States and 10 thousand crore rupees from industry. ITIs provide vocational training to equip youth with practical skills for employment and industry. Under the Craftsmen Training Scheme (CTS), training is offered through Government and Private Industrial Training Institutes in engineering and non-engineering trades. Its course duration varies from six months to two years, depending on the trade. The Directorate General of Training is the apex organisation responsible for the development and coordination of vocational training at the national level. The total number of ITIs, including Government and Private, in the country has increased to over 13 thousand in 2026 from over nine thousand in 2014, indicating an increase of 42 percent. Further, enrolment in ITIs across the country has also increased to 14.70 lakh in the academic session 2025-26 from 9.51 lakh in the academic session 2014-15, indicating an increase of 54 percent. At the national level, the Ministry has constituted a National Steering Committee (NSC) to provide overall direction for the scheme. Since its implementation, 850 ITIs have been identified, comprising 172 Hub ITIs and 678 Spoke ITIs. The NSC has also approved the transition of PM-SETU from its pilot phase to a nationwide rollout across all 200 identified ITI clusters. The rollout enables States and Union Territories to take up implementation based on industry readiness and implementation capacity. Approval has been given to Strategic Investment Plans for 14 ITI clusters under PM-SETU with an investment of over 3 thousand 446 crore rupees.

national_raw_news.title: 5 hours ago | International 280 Saudi Arabia rejects Houthi claim of attack on Riyadh; Yemeni forces say they neutralised hundred...
national_raw_news.content: Saudi Arabia has rejected a Houthi claim that Riyadh was targeted in a missile and drone attack, while Yemeni forces reported heavy losses among Houthi fighters on key fronts in Yemen. Coalition Spokesman of Saudi-led coalition Yemen, Major General Turki Al Malki has rejected the Houthi claim that Riyadh had been targeted, describing it as misleading. The Spokesman has been quoted by Saudi Arabia’s media saying that the Houthis were seeking to project an “illusory victory” amid losses suffered in Taiz – a key front in Yemen. He added that the Houthis are seeking to divert attention from the huge losses that they are suffering. Earlier, Houthi-affiliated channel – Al Masirah, had reported Houthi military spokesman Brig. Gen. Yahya Sare’e saying that they had launched a ballistic missile and drone operation targeting Aramco in Riyadh. Sare’e claimed the strikes hit their targets and caused fires, saying the attack was in response to Saudi airstrikes and missile attacks on Sana’a and other Yemeni provinces. Meanwhile, Saba News Agency in Aden reported that Yemeni armed forces of the internationally recognised government carried out 97 operations against Houthi reinforcements on the Tur al-Bahah and Taiz fronts. It said the operations killed or neutralised 260 Houthi fighters and destroyed or disabled 44 military vehicles and transport and supply assets. The forces have also reportedly struck Houthi targets in Sana’a and Saada, as fighting continues to intensify across the conflict’s important fronts.

national_raw_news.title: Maharashtra Governor Jishnu Dev Varma Highlights Lord Mahavira’s Teachings for Peaceful Society 1 hour ago 26
national_raw_news.content: Maharashtra Governor Jishnu Dev Varma called for forgiveness, non-violence, and universal friendship while highlighting the teachings of Lord Mahavira. Speaking at the Collective Forgiveness, World Friendship Day and Jain Ratna Felicitation Ceremony in Ghatkopar, Mumbai, the Governor said that Jain principles such as truth, non-violence, non-stealing, non-possession and celibacy can help build a peaceful and humane society. He emphasized that forgiveness and friendship should go beyond religious and social boundaries. The Governor also highlighted the Jain philosophy of Anekantavada, which teaches respect for different perspectives and encourages dialogue to resolve conflicts. He described forgiveness as a sign of inner strength and said that Jainism’s compassion extends to all living beings. He also recalled the influence of Jain principles of non-violence on Mahatma Gandhi through his spiritual mentor, Shrimad Rajchandraji. Governor Varma praised the 126-year-old Bharat Jain Mahamandal for its contribution to spiritual values, social unity and humanitarian service. Skill Development Minister Mangalprabhat Lodha urged the Jain community to participate in government welfare and cleanliness initiatives and to support people, farmers and livestock during droughts. During the event, Governor Varma presented Jain Ratna Awards to MLA Parag Shah, Sukharaj Nahar, Kailashchand Jain and Suresh Goyal for their contributions to society. The ceremony was attended by several public representatives, Jain saints, monks, nuns and members of the Bharat Jain Mahamandal.
